- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +1.00 to -0.67), model fails to adjust; apply lag correction: forecast next period = previous forecast - 1–2% of prior deviation.
- In 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; cap forecast at 10% above recent 7-day average to avoid horizon bias.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33), model drifts toward historical mean; use 3-period moving average to anchor forecast.
